question.:question/problem: Which of the following diagrams represents the gradient vector field of the function $f(x,y)=- 3 x - 2 y$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient vector field of a function $f$ is given by $\nabla f.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$f_x(x,y)=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(- 3 x - 2 y)=-3,\qquad f_y(x,y)=\frac{\partial}{\partial y}(- 3 x - 2 y)=-2.$$

So, the gradient vector field is $\nabla f(x,y)=(-3)\,i+(-2)\,j.$

Next, we sketch the vector field at the points $(-2,2)$, $(2,2)$, and $(2,-2)$. Substitute their coordinates into $\nabla f$:

$$\begin{aligned}\nabla f(-2,2)&=(-3)\,i+(-2)\,j \\ \nabla f(2,2)&=(-3)\,i+(-2)\,j \\ \nabla f(2,-2)&=(-3)\,i+(-2)\,j\end{aligned}$$

Now, draw the vectors starting at their corresponding points:

\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{x}^{2}\,i-y\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}∇f(-2,2) & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot (-2)^{2}\,i-2\,j=3\,i-2\,j \\ ∇f(2,-3) & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot {2}^{2}\,i-(-3)\,j=3\,i+3\,j \\ ∇f(2,1) & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot {2}^{2}\,i-\,j=3\,i-j\end{aligned}
